title: Compact all rules and move details into skills
description: Plan for compacting all of .agents/rules while preserving semantics and syncing every reference in the repository.

meta.objective: Compact every .agents/rules/*.md so a rule keeps only its applicability condition, core constraints and links to detailed sources; move procedures, checklists, examples and detailed formats to the appropriate skill or role without changing behavior.
meta.inScope: All rules in .agents/rules; skills, roles, workflows, hook documentation, root instructions, contract, README, config scripts/tests and every affected reference; create/update plan documents and index.
meta.outOfScope: No change to product behavior or CLI, no new policy design, no loosening/tightening of constraints, no dependency installs, no commit/push/deploy, no editing of dirty changes beyond mandatory references, and no implementing the plan content during the planning turn.
meta.currentState: Surveyed the 18 existing rules, the whole .agents/skills tree, Claude/Codex roles, hook docs/scripts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CONTRACT.md, README.md, scripts/check-agent-config.py, package scripts and references via rg. Worktree is dirty: the git-rule merge touches .agents/rules/git.md, CONTRACT.md, git-workflow and hooks; database/dependency audit are also being edited; bin/lumina-agent.mjs and tests/lumina-agent.test.mjs have user changes to protect. docs/plans did not exist before this plan.

assumptions: No HLD/LLD needed since this is a config-documentation refactor with no runtime architecture change.
Prefer extending existing skills/roles; create the coding-standards skill only if the cross-cutting details of coding-principles/comments/type-safety have no single owner without causing duplication.
Session-wide behavioral rules such as response-style, search-priority and simplicity remain rules; only remove examples or move detailed operations, do not force all content into skills.
git.md is currently the dirty result of the immediately preceding request and is the baseline to merge into, not to be replaced by the two deleted rules.
content.technicalSolution: Follow the thin policy layer + operational owner model. Before editing, snapshot each rule into a semantic inventory with trigger, invariant, procedure, checklist, example, output format and every inbound/outbound reference. For each passage: mandatory invariant/authorization/safety/default stays in the rule; procedure/checklist/example/format moves to the skill or role owning the task; purely illustrative content is dropped from the rule after confirming it carries no constraint of its own. Standard mapping: backend→coding-backend (+database/review-web-security when relevant); frontend→coding-frontend (+clone-website/html-to-component); black-box-feature-testing→testcase/testing-strategy/workflow-test and qa-tester-agent; coding-principles/comments/type-safety→coding-backend/coding-frontend/testing-strategy/refactoring-catalog, or a new coding-standards skill if a single cross-cutting owner is needed; data-safety/database-read-only→database/coding-backend/review-web-security; docs-sync/documentation-reading-and-toc→docs (+testcase/workflow-plan for dedicated artifacts); git→git-workflow/workflow-git and hook docs; implementation→workflow-implement/coding-agent; mandatory-report→report/workflow-report; plan-format→workflow-plan/planner-agent/docs template; quality-assurance→testing-strategy/testcase/workflow-test/workflow-review; search-priority→researcher-agent/system-understanding but keep the no-fabrication/local-first core in the rule; simplicity→workflow-implement/refactoring/design skills but keep the scope authorization core in the rule; response-style keeps its core in the rule and moves report-specific format to report. Do not rename/delete a rule while it is still a public target; prefer stable paths to reduce reference migration. After moving, scan the whole repo to fix genuinely wrong links/wording, not files just because they have still-valid links. No data/API/migration. Roll back per cluster with scoped diffs; absolutely never reset the worktree and never restore commit-discipline.md or pull-request-conflict.md, which were merged into git.md.

remainingRisks.description: Over-shrinking rules may stop skills from auto-triggering, leaving constraints no longer loaded session-wide.
remainingRisks.mitigation: Keep every authorization/safety/default invariant in the rule; skills own only procedure/checklist/example and rules have clear pointers/triggers.

remainingRisks.description: Details duplicated across rule, skill and role may drift in wording after moving.
remainingRisks.mitigation: Pick a single owner per the mapping, turn other sources into pointers, then scan the semantics-defining sentences before/after.

remainingRisks.description: The dirty worktree may be overwritten, especially the Git merge batch and bin/tests changes outside the task.
remainingRisks.mitigation: Snapshot the baseline diff per path, edit in small hunks, no reset/checkout, do not restore deleted files and a final diff comparison is mandatory.

remainingRisks.description: Creating an unnecessary coding-standards skill may increase the number of sources and contradict the goal of brevity.
remainingRisks.mitigation: Create it only after the inventory if no existing owner exists; if created, other skills point to it instead of copying content.

remainingRisks.description: Repo tests may fail from pre-existing dirty changes or the environment, not the documentation refactor.
remainingRisks.mitigation: Run real checks, save output, separate baseline errors from diff-caused errors and do not fix errors outside scope.
